data.source_title: Impact of Automated Alerts on Follow-Up of Post-Discharge Microbiology Results: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
data.locator: Abstract, Key Results; Methods, design and measures
data.source_setting: 777-bed academic hospital, Boston; positive under/untreated microbiology results after discharge
data.source_n: 157 results from patients of 121 physicians (intervention 97; control 60)
data.quantity: Documented follow-up within 3 days of post-discharge microbiology result
data.value: 27/97 (28%) intervention vs 8/60 (13%) control; adjusted OR 3.2 (95% CI 1.3-8.4), p=0.01
data.source_evidence_basis: Cluster randomized alert trial; outcome documentation within 3 days.
data.limitations: Single site; physician ID odd/even pseudo-random allocation; follow-up remained low; documented care only. DOI intentionally omitted pending verification.
data.inferred_scenario_use: A callback/result workflow should assign a named owner, alert, acknowledgment, patient/provider communication, action, and escalation; alerts alone do not close every loop.
